datatype.name: FrequencyHz
datatype.definition: A frequency in hertz (cycles per second). Modelled as a local datatype rather than a wmoop.core quantity because the core kernel defines no Frequency QuantityKind; the standard tuning reference is A4 = 440 Hz.

provenance.source: ISO 16:1975, Acoustics — Standard tuning frequency (Standard musical pitch)

datatype.name: MidiNoteNumber
datatype.definition: A MIDI note number 0-127; middle C (C4) is 60 and A4 (440 Hz) is 69.

provenance.source: MIDI 1.0 Detailed Specification, MIDI Manufacturers Association

datatype.name: Semitones
datatype.definition: A count of semitones (half steps), the smallest interval in twelve-tone equal temperament.

concept.name: PitchClass
concept.definition: One of the twelve pitch classes of the chromatic scale (C, C#, D, …), each the set of all pitches an whole number of octaves apart; an abstract entity independent of octave or instrument.

provenance.note: Twelve-tone equal temperament; the member pitch classes are enumerated as L2 individuals.

concept.name: Interval
concept.definition: The pitch distance between two notes, measured in semitones.

provenance.note: Interval sizes in semitones are a convention of twelve-tone equal temperament.

property.name: semitones
property.definition: The width of the interval in semitones (e.g. 7 for a perfect fifth, 12 for an octave).

concept.name: Scale
concept.definition: An ordered collection of pitch classes spanning an octave, from which the pitch material of a passage is drawn (e.g. the major scale). A Collection of pitch classes (membership, not mereological parthood).

provenance.note: An L0 Collection whose members are pitch classes.

relation.name: hasPitchClass
relation.definition: A pitch class that is a member of this scale.

concept.name: Chord
concept.definition: A set of three or more pitch classes conceived as sounding together. A Collection of pitch classes (an abstract harmonic object).

provenance.note: An L0 Collection whose members are pitch classes; sounded simultaneously.

relation.name: hasPitchClass
relation.definition: A pitch class that is a member of this chord.

concept.name: MusicalWork
concept.definition: An abstract musical composition — the work itself, as distinct from any particular performance or recording of it (a C# in it is the same work's note in every performance).

provenance.note: The work/performance distinction: a MusicalWork is abstract (category C); its performances are perdurants (category B).

property.name: title
property.definition: The title by which the work is known.

concept.name: MusicalInstrument
concept.definition: A device constructed or adapted to produce musical sound.

provenance.source: Hornbostel, E. M. von & Sachs, C. (1914), Systematik der Musikinstrumente, Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 46
provenance.ref: the classification of instruments by sound-producing mechanism

concept.name: Idiophone
concept.definition: An instrument that produces sound by the vibration of its own rigid body, without strings or a membrane (e.g. a xylophone, a bell).

provenance.source: Hornbostel, E. M. von & Sachs, C. (1914), Systematik der Musikinstrumente, Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 46

concept.name: Membranophone
concept.definition: An instrument that produces sound by the vibration of a stretched membrane (e.g. a drum).

provenance.source: Hornbostel, E. M. von & Sachs, C. (1914), Systematik der Musikinstrumente, Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 46

concept.name: Chordophone
concept.definition: An instrument that produces sound by the vibration of one or more stretched strings (e.g. a violin, a piano).

provenance.source: Hornbostel, E. M. von & Sachs, C. (1914), Systematik der Musikinstrumente, Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 46

concept.name: Aerophone
concept.definition: An instrument that produces sound by a vibrating column or body of air (e.g. a flute, a trumpet).

provenance.source: Hornbostel, E. M. von & Sachs, C. (1914), Systematik der Musikinstrumente, Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 46

concept.name: Electrophone
concept.definition: An instrument in which sound is generated or primarily produced by electrical or electronic means (e.g. a synthesizer).

provenance.source: Sachs, C. (1940), The History of Musical Instruments, W. W. Norton
provenance.ref: class 5, Electrophones (added to the 1914 Hornbostel-Sachs scheme)

concept.name: MusicalPerformance
concept.definition: A particular event of performing music: a rendering, bounded in time, of a musical work (or an improvisation), made up of note occurrences.

provenance.note: An occurrent/event (category B) with temporal parts (its NoteOccurrences), distinct from the abstract MusicalWork it renders.

relation.name: performs
relation.definition: The musical work this performance renders (absent for a free improvisation).

relation.name: performedOn
relation.definition: An instrument used in this performance.

concept.name: NoteOccurrence
concept.definition: A single sounded note within a performance: the event of a pitch class being sounded for a span of time. The concrete, in-time counterpart of the abstract pitch class.

provenance.note: Resolves the 'a note is both a type and an event' problem: PitchClass is abstract (category C); NoteOccurrence is the perdurant (category B) that sounds it.

relation.name: soundsPitchClass
relation.definition: The pitch class this occurrence sounds.

relation.name: partOf
relation.definition: The performance this note occurrence is a part of.

role.name: Performer
role.definition: The role of a person who performs music.

provenance.note: An agentive, contextual facet of a Person — a role, not a kind of Person.

individual.name: C#
individual.definition: The pitch class C sharp / D flat.

individual.name: D#
individual.definition: The pitch class D sharp / E flat.

individual.name: F#
individual.definition: The pitch class F sharp / G flat.

individual.name: G#
individual.definition: The pitch class G sharp / A flat.

individual.name: A
individual.definition: The pitch class A; A4 is the 440 Hz tuning reference (ISO 16).

individual.name: A#
individual.definition: The pitch class A sharp / B flat.

individual.name: PerfectUnison
individual.definition: The interval of zero semitones — two notes of the same pitch.

individual.name: Octave
individual.definition: The interval of twelve semitones, spanning one full pitch-class cycle.

individual.name: Violin
individual.definition: A four-stringed bowed chordophone of the violin family.

provenance.source: Hornbostel, E. M. von & Sachs, C. (1914), Systematik der Musikinstrumente, Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 46

individual.name: Flute
individual.definition: An edge-blown woodwind aerophone sounded by directing air across an opening.

provenance.source: Hornbostel, E. M. von & Sachs, C. (1914), Systematik der Musikinstrumente, Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 46

individual.name: SnareDrum
individual.definition: A membranophone with a struck head and snares that rattle against it.

provenance.source: Hornbostel, E. M. von & Sachs, C. (1914), Systematik der Musikinstrumente, Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 46
